# APS formats (contracts)

Change these only after telling the whole team.

## Canonical JSON

```python
json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode()
```

All signatures are Ed25519 over canonical JSON. Keys and signatures are base64.
Implementation: `aps/canonical.py`.

## Registry record (`data/registry.json`, generated by `scripts/issue_seals.py`)

```json
{
  "node_id": "ch.basel.hotel-rheinblick",
  "name": "Hotel Rheinblick",
  "uid": "CHE-526.018.151",
  "public_key": "<base64 ed25519 verify key>",
  "endpoint": "http://localhost:4001",
  "kind": "business",
  "capabilities": ["can_book", "can_take_payment"],
  "tags": ["hotel", "basel-sbb", "dog-friendly"],
  "seals": [
    { "issuer": "handelsregister-bs", "tier": "gold", "signature": "<b64>" },
    { "issuer": "adobe", "tier": "blue", "signature": "<b64>" }
  ]
}
```

Each seal signature = issuer's key over canonical
`{"node_id", "uid", "public_key", "capabilities", "issuer", "tier"}`.

`uid` is the Swiss business identification number, `CHE-ddd.ddd.ddd` with a mod-11 check
digit (eCH-0097, `aps/uid.py`), or `null` for nodes without one. It is always signed, so it
cannot be added, changed or removed after sealing.

## Signed envelope (every tool and agent response)

```json
{
  "node_id": "ch.basel.hotel-rheinblick",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-14T00:12:00Z",
  "payload": { "...": "..." },
  "signature": "<node key over canonical {node_id, timestamp, payload}>"
}
```

`timestamp` is UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. A receiver that needs a live answer also checks
freshness (`verify_envelope(..., max_age_s=...)`): at most `max_age_s` old and at most 60 s
in the future (clock skew). The assistant drops node replies older than 300 s as possible
replays. Envelopes kept on purpose (commitments redeemed at `book`) are checked without
`max_age_s`; they carry their own `valid_until`.

## Trust tiers and seal rules (`aps/seals.py`)

| Tier | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| gold | issued by a government authority (handelsregister-bs, bar-association-ch) |
| blue | issued by a company registry (adobe) or a platform |
| grey | self-signed or unsigned ("untrusted"); exists, low weight, never enough for payments or licensed capabilities |
| broken | a claimed seal or the envelope does not verify; content is dropped |

- A seal is valid only if its issuer is in `data/authorities.json`, the claimed tier
  equals the authority's tier, and the signature verifies with the authority's key.
- A seal whose `issuer` equals the node's own `node_id` is self-signed: valid only
  with tier `grey`, verified with the node's own public key.
- If **any** claimed seal is invalid, the node is `broken`. Otherwise its tier is the
  highest tier among its seals; a node with no seals at all is `grey` (unsigned).
- Licensed capabilities (listed under an authority's `licenses`, e.g.
  `licensed_legal_ch` for `bar-association-ch`) are granted only with a valid seal
  from that authority. `can_take_payment` needs tier blue or higher.
- A seal from an authority with `"vouches_for_uid": true` (the commercial register) is
  valid only if the record has a valid `uid`. The verdict's `uid` is set only through such
  a seal; any other `uid` in a record is just a claim.

## Authorities (`data/authorities.json`)

```json
[{ "issuer": "bar-association-ch", "name": "...", "tier": "gold",
   "licenses": ["licensed_legal_ch"], "public_key": "<b64>" },
 { "issuer": "handelsregister-bs", "name": "...", "tier": "gold",
   "vouches_for_uid": true, "public_key": "<b64>" }]
```

`public_key` is filled in by `scripts/gen_keys.py`.

## Node config (`data/nodes/*.json`, hand written)

```json
{
  "node_id": "...", "name": "...", "uid": "CHE-ddd.ddd.ddd (optional)", "port": 4001, "kind": "business",
  "capabilities": [...], "tags": [...],
  "seals": [{ "issuer": "adobe", "tier": "blue" }],
  "facts": { "...": "everything the node's tools and agent may answer from" }
}
```

`facts.add_ons` lists what the node's A2A agent may commit to:
`[{ "id", "item", "price_chf", "conditions": [...] }]`. The node's LLM only picks an add-on
id; the signed commitment (item, price, conditions, valid_until) is built from the config.

`facts.profile` says who the business is, so small businesses are visibly comparable to
big ones: `{ "size": "large | medium | small", "rooms_total", "about",
"chain"? }`. It is public: `get_policies` and the agent card return it, and the node's agent may
talk about it. The persona (`agent.persona`) only says who the *agent* is, not the business.

`facts.negotiation = { "floor_chf", "max_rounds" }` holds the owner's limits. It is
**private**: listed in `PRIVATE_FACTS` (`node/agent.py`), never put in an LLM prompt and
never returned by any tool; only the node's own code may use it.

In `seals`, `"issuer": "self"` means a self-signed grey seal, and
`"signed_by": "self"` makes the node sign a seal in someone else's name (the scam).

## Key files (`keys/<key_id>.json`)

`{"key_id", "public_key", "private_key"}`, base64; private key is the 32-byte seed.
Key ids: authority issuer ids, node ids, user agent ids (e.g. `ch.tuttie.alex-muster`) and
`user` (the person: signs approvals and delegations).

## UI event (assistant → UI over SSE)

```json
{
  "step": 3,
  "kind": "registry | a2t | a2a | marketplace | payment | approval | answer | thinking",
  "node_id": "ch.basel.hotel-rheinblick",
  "node_name": "Hotel Rheinblick",
  "seals": [{ "issuer": "handelsregister-bs", "tier": "gold", "valid": true }],
  "status": "verified | untrusted | broken | pending | approved | declined | info",
  "summary": "get_availability: double room 14 Nov, CHF 180",
  "detail": {}
}
```

`untrusted` marks a node whose seals are valid but only grey (self-signed or unsigned).
`thinking` events carry a reasoning summary of the assistant's LLM in `summary`
(usually `"**Title**\n\nbody"`), with `status: "info"` and no node. The SSE stream also
sends a named `reset` event when a new demo starts; the UI then clears itself.
`answer` events carry `detail.mood`, how the answer feels (one of `MOODS` in
`assistant/agent.py`, e.g. `excited`, `sorry`); the wallet shows it on Tuttie's face.

## A2A reply (structured, never free text)

```json
{
  "answer": "Yes, late arrival with a dog is fine.",
  "commitment": {
    "item": "late check-in 01:00 with dog",
    "price_chf": 15,
    "conditions": ["key box at entrance", "dog fee CHF 15 per night"],
    "valid_until": "2026-11-14T03:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

Wrapped in a signed envelope. The assistant treats other agents' text as data, never
as instructions.

## User agent and delegation (`data/agents/*.json`, `aps/delegation.py`)

A user agent (Tuttie) is in the registry like a node, with `"kind": "user-agent"`, its own
key and seals (the platform seals it, e.g. `adobe`/blue), and the endpoint of the assistant.
Its config has no `facts` and no node server; instead it carries a delegation request
`{"scopes": [...], "valid_days": 365}`, and its registry record gets a **delegation**
signed by the `user` key:

```json
{
  "agent_id": "ch.tuttie.alex-muster",
  "agent_public_key": "<b64, must equal the record's public_key>",
  "scopes": ["ask_agents", "negotiate", "post_requests"],
  "issued_at": "2026-10-31T12:00:00Z",
  "expires_at": "2027-10-31T12:00:00Z",
  "signature": "<user key over canonical {agent_id, agent_public_key, scopes, issued_at, expires_at}>"
}
```

A delegation is valid only for the agent id and key in its own registry record, until
`expires_at`, and only for its scopes (`ask_agents`, `negotiate`, `post_requests`). Paying
is not a scope: every payment still needs the user's signed approval (below). The
assistant serves its own checked identity at `GET /identity`
(`{node_id, name, trust_tier, verified_by, capabilities, acts_for_user, scopes, ...}`).

## Approval

Assistant creates `{id, action, payee_node_id, amount_chf, summary, seals}`; the phone
page lists pending approvals, the user taps Approve/Decline; the decision is signed
with the user's key and attached to the action (e.g. passed to `book`).

## DRAFT: marketplace messages (Tuttie, issues #8 #10)

Proposal so the marketplace, node and wallet work can start in parallel. **Not fully agreed
by the team yet; the marketplace agent layer is built against this draft** (decision to save
time until Sunday 12:00). The source of truth is `code/marketplace/messages.py` (strict
Pydantic models, unknown fields are refused); change both together. Every message below is the `payload` of a
signed envelope (see above), signed by its sender: the user's agent with its own key (its
delegation proves it acts for the user),
business agents with their node key.

### Request (user's agent → marketplace)

```json
{
  "type": "request",
  "request_id": "rq-7f3a",
  "category": "hotel",
  "tags": ["basel-sbb"],
  "constraints": {
    "date": "2026-11-14",
    "guests": 1,
    "budget_chf": 200,
    "requirements": ["quiet", "dog", "arrival 01:00"]
  },
  "expires_at": "2026-11-13T20:00:00Z"
}
```

Only public information goes into a request: every matching business sees it. `guests`
defaults to 1; `budget_chf` and `requirements` are optional.

### Posting and wake-up (marketplace → business agent)

When the marketplace accepts a request it wakes every matching, non-broken business at
`POST {endpoint}/agent/invoke` with:

```json
{
  "type": "posting.created",
  "posting": {
    "request_id": "rq-7f3a",
    "requester_id": "ch.tuttie.alex-muster",
    "request": { "...": "the user agent's signed envelope, unchanged" },
    "offer_url": "http://localhost:4010/postings/rq-7f3a/offers",
    "expires_at": "2026-11-13T20:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

The business can verify the requester itself from `request` (seals, signature, delegation).
Its answer, e.g. `{"interested": true, "next_tool": "make_offer"}` (plain or as the payload
of a signed envelope), is recorded but advisory; only a signed offer counts.

### Offer (business agent → user's agent)

```json
{
  "type": "offer",
  "request_id": "rq-7f3a",
  "offer_id": "of-rheinblick-1",
  "item": "double room 14 Nov",
  "price_chf": 195,
  "includes": ["late check-in after 22:00 with dog"],
  "conditions": ["non-refundable"],
  "valid_until": "2026-11-13T22:00:00Z"
}
```

Prices come from the node config (`facts.rooms`, `facts.add_ons`), never from an LLM.
Sent as a signed envelope to the posting's `offer_url`. The marketplace accepts it only from
an invited business, fresh (≤ 300 s), for this `request_id` and before `valid_until`.

### Marketplace API (port 4010)

| Call | Body / answer |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /postings` | signed request envelope → `{request_id, posting, request, invited: {node_id: {name, trust_tier, status, next_tool}}, offers}` |
| `POST /postings/{id}/offers` | signed offer envelope → `{node_id, name, trust_tier, uid, offer, within_budget, envelope}` |
| `GET /postings/{id}` | the posting with `invited` and all accepted `offers` |
| `GET /postings/{id}/shortlist` | best five current offers within budget: by price, grey last |

`status` is `interested`, `declined`, `invited` (no clear answer) or `unreachable`.
Refusals: `{"refused": true, "reason"}` with 403, 404, 409, 410 or 422.

### Counter-offer (either side, during negotiation; implemented in `code/negotiation/`)

```json
{
  "type": "counter",
  "offer_id": "of-rheinblick-1",
  "round": 2,
  "price_chf": 185,
  "includes": ["late check-in after 22:00 with dog"],
  "conditions": ["non-refundable"],
  "final": false
}
```

Only the price is negotiable: `includes` and `conditions` must equal the offer's. Round 1 is
the guest's first counter; the business answers every round with a Counter of the same round,
an Agreement or a Rejection. `final: true` (business only) marks its last price: after that
the guest can only accept it (a counter at that price) or walk away.

### Agreement (business → guest agent, signed by the business)

```json
{
  "type": "agreement", "request_id": "rq-7f3a", "offer_id": "of-rheinblick-1", "round": 2,
  "item": "double room 2026-11-14", "price_chf": 185,
  "includes": ["late check-in after 22:00 with dog"], "conditions": ["non-refundable"],
  "valid_until": "2026-11-13T22:00:00Z"
}
```

The price both sides accept. It is what the user approves on the phone (see Approval) and
what booking redeems instead of the list price (`negotiation/agreement.py`,
`AgreementRedeemer`): only with this hotel's own signature, before `valid_until`, and only
once per `offer_id`; the user's approval must be for exactly `price_chf`. `book` takes it as
an optional `agreement` field once the hook in `node/server.py` is in.

### Rejection (business → guest agent)

`{"type": "rejection", "offer_id", "round", "reason"}`: the business ends the negotiation
(fixed prices, its final price was not accepted, or no rounds left); its offer still stands.

### `counter_offer` tool (every node, `POST /tools/counter_offer`)

Stateless, like `book`: each call carries everything the hotel needs, each part signed by
whoever is responsible for it.

```json
{
  "counter": "<the user agent's signed envelope, payload: Counter>",
  "offer":   "<this hotel's own signed Offer envelope>",
  "last":    "<this hotel's own signed previous Counter envelope, null in round 1>"
}
```

The hotel checks: the offer and `last` carry its own signature (so nobody can make it
"remember" a price it never proposed), the offer is still valid, the counter comes from a
sealed user agent whose delegation grants `negotiate`, is fresh (≤ 300 s) and belongs to
this offer and round. The answer is a signed `{"tool": "counter_offer", ...Counter |
Agreement | Rejection}`, or `{"tool": "counter_offer", "status": "refused", "reason"}`.

**Limits** (`negotiation/rules.py`, compared in code only): `facts.negotiation =
{"floor_chf", "max_rounds"}` is private, never sent and never in a prompt. `floor_chf` is the
lowest price for the standard room (`double`, else the cheapest); other rooms may drop by
the same share; add-ons are never discounted. The hotel meets the guest halfway, never below
its floor, and its price is final in the last round or once it reaches the floor.

**Tuttie's side** (`negotiation/tuttie.py`): one subagent per offer, all in parallel, each in
its own session. The user's real limit is the private context item `max_price_chf`: compared
in Tuttie's code, never shared or sent. Tuttie opens 10 % below the offer, then moves halfway
toward the hotel's price, accepts a final or close price within the limit and walks away
otherwise. The cheapest Agreement is what the user approves.

**Strategy numbers** (tuned for the demo; preview with `scripts/bargain_preview.py`):
`OPENING_DISCOUNT = 0.10` and `TUTTIE_STEP = 0.5` (`negotiation/tuttie.py`), `HOTEL_STEP =
0.34` (`negotiation/rules.py`: the hotel moves a third of the way toward the guest). Pitch
story (`documentation/context/pitch/storyline.md`), pinned by a test: Gästehaus am Rhein
double with late arrival and dog at CHF 135, budget 160 → Tuttie 121 → Anna 131 → Tuttie 126
→ Anna 130 → Tuttie 128 → agreed at CHF 128 (three rounds, above Anna's floor, never at it).
Rheinblick double + dog at CHF 195, budget 200: 175 → 189 → 182 → 187 → agreed at 185.

**No `negotiation.counter` wake-up:** counters go straight to the signed `counter_offer` tool,
which answers each round at once, so the marketplace never sends this event.

## Business agent (implemented, issue #10)

Every company on the agent web has the same agent object, in the `agent` section of its node
config (`code/data/nodes/*.json`, code in `code/node/agent.py`):

```json
"agent": {
  "persona": {
    "name": "Lena", "role": "reservations agent", "tone": "how the agent speaks",
    "priorities": ["what it tries to achieve"], "boundaries": ["what it must never do"]
  },
  "tools": ["get_availability", "get_policies", "book", "make_offer", "counter_offer", "pay"],
  "wakes_on": ["posting.created", "posting.updated"]
}
```

Tools come from the shared catalog `code/node/catalog.py`; each has a status, `available` or
`planned` (`make_offer`, `counter_offer` and `pay` are planned). Private negotiation limits
live in `facts.negotiation` and never reach a prompt, a reply or the card.

Endpoints of every node (all answers are signed envelopes):

| Endpoint | Payload of the answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /agent/card` | `{node_id, business, profile, persona (without boundaries), tools {name: {status, endpoint, description}}, wakes_on, invoke}`; the marketplace reads it to check the subscription |
| `POST /agent` `{question, context}` | A2A reply `{answer, commitment}` (see above) |
| `POST /agent/invoke` with the event itself as body | `{woken_by, interested, reason, next_tool, next_tool_available}`, or `{woken_by, ignored: true, reason}` for events the agent does not subscribe to. If interested in a `posting.created` with `next_tool: make_offer`, the node then sends a signed `Offer` to the posting's `offer_url` in the background |

`event` is a marketplace event, e.g. `{"type": "posting.created", "posting": {...}}`
(postings: see "DRAFT: marketplace messages"). The marketplace will wake the agents
subscribed to an event; an interested agent then uses `next_tool`, e.g. `make_offer` once it
exists.

## Sessions and context passing (implemented)

Agents that talk over several turns (a Tuttie subagent and a hotel, later a negotiation) open a
**session**. Each side keeps its own memory of it (`code/sessions/memory.py`), so many
sessions run in parallel without mixing. Endpoints of every node (answers are signed):

| Endpoint | Payload of the answer |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /agent/sessions` `{peer, purpose, context}` | `{session_id, agent, purpose}` |
| `POST /agent/sessions/{id}/messages` `{message}` | `{session_id, turn, answer, commitment}`; the agent sees the session's history |
| `GET /agent/sessions/{id}` | the whole session: `{session_id, owner, peer, purpose, status, context, state, turns: [{author, kind, content, at}]}` |
| `POST /agent/sessions/{id}/close` | `{session_id, status: "closed"}`; later messages get HTTP 409 |

`context` is what the opening agent chose to share. Every item an agent holds has a
visibility (`code/sessions/context.py`): `public` (may go into a posting), `negotiation` (may
go to the one business it talks to) or `private` (never leaves the agent; the default).
Agents only ever send `Context.share(up_to=...)`, which can never include private items.
